clue.text: That old shake-down by the golden gate for instance

definitions.text: That old shake-down by the golden gate for instance

parts.words: That old shake-down by the golden gate for instance
parts.note: the famous shaking of San Francisco, the city on the Golden Gate strait, in 1906

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look back at some old swindle pulled off near a golden gateway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shake-down' suggests extortion, but here it is literal: the ground shaking down buildings beside the Golden Gate, the strait at San Francisco, in 1906.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1906 San Francisco disaster is the classic example of a violent tremor of the ground.

clue.text: It makes a girl go without a single movement

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for go sits around the single

parts.note: taken as written
a single is one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Something makes a girl leave without moving a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here: GO goes round I. The definition is a musical movement, a slow one.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow section of a symphony or sonata is often marked with this tempo, so it names a movement.

clue.text: With, in the driver's place, entire immunity from breathalyzers

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase, the answer an adjective: a non-drinker has nothing to fear from the test

parts.note: a golfer's driver is used from the tee
total means entire, complete

explanation.surface: A driver who has full immunity from roadside breath tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist, but it is the golf club, struck from a tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never drinks alcohol has nothing to fear from a police breath test.

clue.text: When the poor tenant begs for mercy?

definitions.text: When the poor tenant begs for mercy?

parts.words: When the poor tenant begs for mercy
parts.note: mercy in battle is quarter; the date when rent falls due is when a hard-up tenant needs it

explanation.surface: A question about the moment an impoverished tenant pleads for leniency.
explanation.walkthrough: In England rent was traditionally paid on four fixed days a year, such as Lady Day and Michaelmas; 'quarter' is also mercy given to a beaten foe.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the four dates in the English year when rents and dues are paid has this name.

clue.text: This case has a 3 pain

parts.note: points to the answer at 3 down, total abstinence from drink, abbreviated TT
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A case that has three pains.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' refers to 3 down, a word for one who abstains, whose usual abbreviation TT stands for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim briefcase for documents is named after the diplomatic official who carried one.

clue.text: 'e's 'ot, this lad-but that's secret

indicators.note: but here means except: the secret word without the dropped-aitch start

parts.note: esoteric means secret, understood only by an inner circle
he's hot said with the aitches dropped, giving the letters E S O T

explanation.surface: A lad says he is hot but keeps it secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'e's 'ot plus this lad as one word meaning secret; take away the cockney he's hot and the lad's name is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a boy's name, so it names a lad.

clue.text: Underworld chief soundly tricked by this commissioner?

definitions.note: the answer is the first word of the colonial title district commissioner

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so tricked is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: tricked sounds like the letters TRICT

explanation.surface: A crime boss thoroughly fooled by a colonial official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld chief' suggests a gangster but is the god Dis. 'Soundly' looks like thoroughly but signals the homophone of 'tricked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonial district commissioner governed an administrative area, so this word completes his title.

clue.text: Shared by some under-secretaries with Tennyson's brook

definitions.text: Shared by some under-secretaries with Tennyson's brook

parts.words: Shared by some under-secretaries with Tennyson's brook
parts.note: British civil service has permanent under-secretaries, and Tennyson's brook says 'I go on for ever'

explanation.surface: Something civil servants have in common with a poet's stream.
explanation.walkthrough: A Permanent Under-Secretary is the top civil servant in a British ministry; Tennyson's poem The Brook has the refrain 'men may come and men may go, but I go on for ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting for ever, the brook's boast, and the fixed tenure of senior civil servants both show enduring quality.

clue.text: Fret about a tree.

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand for about, concerning
a pine is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: Someone worrying over the health of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to grieve or complain discontentedly, a synonym.

clue.text: Secure way to train a sprinter by stopping his food?

definitions.meaning: to fasten or tie up firmly

definitions.text: way to train a sprinter by stopping his food?
definitions.meaning: read as a coaching method: cause the runner to go without eating while also making him quick

explanation.surface: A dependable training regime for a runner that involves cutting off his meals.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: a sailor's term for tying up securely, and, taken literally, both 'make (him) fast' as in quick and 'make (him) fast' as in go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie a rope or boat firmly is to secure it; starving someone forces abstinence while speed is the trainer's goal.

clue.text: Get used to Muscat Company formation

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so the letters of Muscat and the company are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm in the capital of Oman settling into local ways as it forms.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSCAT with CO rearranged gives the answer; 'formation' looks like part of a business phrase but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To habituate someone, to make familiar by habit, is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Cheer for Elihu

definitions.meaning: in American usage, to cheer for a team or candidate
Elihu ..., American Secretary of State and Nobel Peace Prize winner

explanation.definitionFit: Americans shout support for a side using this verb; the statesman Elihu bore this surname.

clue.text: Engineer overrides innkeeper — far from democratic

indicators.note: in a down clue, riding over means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps
a publican keeps a public house

explanation.surface: An engineer overrules a pub landlord, hardly a democratic act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from democratic' plays on the two US parties: the answer is the Democrats' opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: In US politics the party opposed to the Democrats is the GOP, so its member is the opposite of a Democrat.

clue.text: Something for a scholar ? Good show !

definitions.meaning: in British universities and schools an award of money to a pupil, smaller than a scholarship
a public display of works, as in a gallery

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this word also names a minor scholarship grant at a school or college, which is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A student's bursary at Oxford or Cambridge has this name, as does a public display in a gallery.

clue.text: Metamorphosis of a gentleman-ranker

parts.note: Kipling's poem Gentlemen-Rankers calls disgraced gentlemen serving in the ranks 'little lambs who have lost our way' who went astray

explanation.surface: A transformation that overtakes a well-born private soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A gentleman-ranker was a man of good family enlisted as a private, often after disgrace; Kipling's poem has them bleating 'Baa! Baa! Baa!' as lost sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A family's disgraced member, the one who has gone astray, is called this, as Kipling's ruined gentlemen were.

clue.text: Introduction barred

parts.note: an opening piece of music, written out in bars, rather than an introduction that has been refused

explanation.surface: Someone has been refused entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred' suggests forbidden, but it means set out in musical bars: an opening movement before a fugue or a longer work.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the introductory movement before a larger piece goes by this name.

clue.text: A fellow holds a thousand in school in N. London

indicators.note: in shows the fellow with his thousand goes inside the school

parts.note: Eton, the English public school

indicators.note: the fellow holds, contains, the thousand within him

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A college fellow keeps a thousand pupils at a school in north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English boarding school; it opens to take DON, which itself holds M. Edmonton is a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: This district lies in the north of the capital, in the borough of Enfield.

clue.text: Dramatist meets Moor in battle

definitions.meaning: ... Moor, the 1644 English Civil War battle near York, where this name is joined to Moor

explanation.surface: A playwright confronts an Othello-like figure in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' suggests Othello, but it is the moorland in the name of the Civil War battle of 1644.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright of The Malcontent shares his surname with the village beside the moor where the Civil War battle was fought.

clue.text: The way pop fans reacted made me scared

indicators.note: made signals that the letters of me scared are made into something else

explanation.surface: Something about pop fans' reaction frightened me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is the anagram signal: ME SCARED rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterical fans at pop concerts famously yelled at full pitch, which is this reaction.

clue.text: Song about a topless bust in the country

indicators.note: about means around, so the song encloses the rest

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: topless means losing the top letter, here the first of bust

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ditty about a bare-chested statue in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless bust' paints a racy picture, but 'topless' just removes the first letter, and 'about' puts the song around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is a European republic, Vienna its capital.

clue.text: Indian flying fish ?

parts.note: a dried fish eaten in India, whose name includes a bird; the bird name makes it seem able to fly

explanation.surface: A question about a fish of the subcontinent that can fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The bummalo, a small fish of the Mumbai coast often dried and served as a relish, has a name ending in a bird, hence 'flying'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bummalo, a small fish of western India sold dried, is known by this name which pairs the city with a waterbird.

clue.text: National nation

definitions.meaning: the Grand National, Britain's famous steeplechase run at Aintree

explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is the best-known British horse race, held each spring at Aintree, Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand National is a horse contest; a people of shared ancestry is also called this.

clue.text: Rin's dance ?

parts.note: Rin Tin Tin, the film dog, has tin twice in his name, and a tin is a can, so his dance doubles can

explanation.surface: A question about a dance done by someone called Rin.
explanation.walkthrough: Rin is short for Rin Tin Tin; with tin read as can, Tin Tin becomes the high-kicking Parisian dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The high-kicking French music-hall dance repeats a word for a container, as the dog's name repeats tin.

clue.text: No rating can be so clueless !

indicators.note: says the letters of no rating can be made into another word by rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone without any rating at all could only be lacking in knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' signals that NO RATING may become another word; the answer's letters are exactly those eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking knowledge or awareness is uninformed, a synonym.

clue.text: Play(s) parts

definitions.meaning: performs on stage, or in the plural noun sense the main divisions of a drama
the major divisions of a play

explanation.definitionFit: To perform a role is to do this verb; the main divisions of a drama are its sections, also called this.

clue.text: Pan's office staff down by the river?

parts.note: the god Pan played pipes made from reeds
a mace is a ceremonial staff carried as a symbol of office

explanation.surface: The office workers of a god have gone down to the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office staff' looks like employees but is a ceremonial rod of office. The definition plays on the fluffy seed down of the bulrush that grows by rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulrush, a waterside plant whose seed heads burst into fluff, is also known by this name.

clue.text: One's up on this but how much ?

definitions.meaning: a rider is up on a horse, a mount

explanation.surface: Someone is ahead, but by what margin?
explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads as A MOUNT: one sits up on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantity or sum answers the question of how much; a horse ridden is a mount.

clue.text: Dashing about in a fearfully neat if disorderly fashion?

definitions.text: Dashing about in a fearfully neat if disorderly fashion?

parts.words: Dashing about in a fearfully neat if disorderly fashion
parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is cattle rushing about in panic

explanation.surface: Someone smartly turned out but rushing around in a disordered way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle: a herd charging in fear and confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd of frightened animals rushing headlong is the classic image of this headlong panic.
